'''Oleh Volodymyrovych Blokhin''' ({{langx|uk|Олег Володимирович Блохін}}) or '''Oleg Vladimirovich Blokhin''' ({{langx|ru|Олег Владимирович Блохин}}; born 5 November 1952), is a Ukrainian former [[association football|football]] player and manager. Regarded as one of the greatest footballers of his generation, Blokhin was a standout [[striker (association football)|striker]] for [[Dynamo Kyiv]] and the [[Soviet Union national football team|Soviet Union]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/gallery/50-greatest-footballers-all-time |title=The 50 greatest footballers of all time {{!}} FourFourTwo |date=7 January 2021 |access-date=8 July 2021 |archive-date=28 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210928145436/https://www.fourfourtwo.com/gallery/50-greatest-footballers-all-time |url-status=live }}</ref>

He holds the all-time top goalscorer record for both Dynamo Kyiv (266 goals) and the [[Soviet Union national football team|Soviet Union national team]] (42 goals), as well as being the overall top goalscorer in the history of the [[Soviet Top League]] (211 goals). He is also the only player to have been [[Cap (sport)|capped]] over [[List of men's footballers with 100 or more international caps|100 times]] for the Soviet Union and holds Dynamo's appearance record with 582 appearances during his 18-year spell at the club. With Dynamo, Blokhin won eight [[List of Soviet and Russian football champions|Soviet league titles]], five [[Soviet Cup|national cups]] and two [[European Cup Winners' Cup]]s. He also competed for the Soviet Union at the [[Football at the 1972 Summer Olympics|1972]] and [[Football at the 1976 Summer Olympics|1976]] [[Football at the Summer Olympics|Olympic Games]] and [[1982 FIFA World Cup|1982]] and [[1986 FIFA World Cup|1986]] [[FIFA World Cup]]s. During his playing career he won the [[Soviet Footballer of the Year]] award three times and the [[Ukrainian Footballer of the Year]] award nine times (both records). In 1975, he was named European Footballer of the Year, winning the [[Ballon d'Or]], becoming the second Soviet and the first Ukrainian player to achieve such a feat.

As a coach, he has had two spells in charge of the [[Ukraine national football team|Ukraine national team]], managing the team at the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]] and [[UEFA Euro 2012]].

In 2011, Blokhin, together with [[Igor Belanov]] and [[Vitaliy Starukhin]], were named as "the legends of Ukrainian football" at the Victory of Football awards.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bulvar.com.ua/gazeta/archive/s51_65095/7221.html|title=Лучшими футболистами Украины признаны Анатолий Тимощук, Андрей Шевченко и Александр Шовковский|work=Bulvar Gordona|author=Dvali, Natalia|date=22 December 2011|access-date=25 September 2020|archive-date=25 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190725072717/http://bulvar.com.ua/gazeta/archive/s51_65095/7221.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Blokhin was born in [[Kyiv]], the capital of the [[Ukrainian SSR]], in 1952. His mother [[Kateryna Adamenko]] was multiple champion of USSR in the [[Women's pentathlon|pentathlon]], sprint and [[long jump]]. He was born to a Russian father and Ukrainian mother. His father [[:ru:Блохин, Владимир Иванович|Vladimir Blokhin]] was a police officer, a World War II veteran, and a competitive sprinter. Owing to his parents, Blokhin quickly mastered sprint, and by the age of 16 ran 60 m in less than 7 seconds, and 100 m in 11.0 seconds.<ref>[https://www.sports.ru/tribuna/blogs/kleshchonok/2770954.html Блохин и Беланов – главные спринтеры в истории футбола. Пиковый Блохин считался опаснее Кройффа и стоил как Марадона] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210521005846/https://www.sports.ru/tribuna/blogs/kleshchonok/2770954.html |date=21 May 2021 }}. sports.ru. 27 April 2008</ref>

== Playing career ==
Blokhin played for Dynamo Kyiv during the 1970s. He became the highest goalscorer in the Soviet League. Typically a forward or winger, Blokhin was noted for his pace.

Blokhin played during most of his career for Dynamo Kyiv, becoming the [[Soviet Union|USSR]] national championship's all-time leader and goalscorer with 211 goals, as well as making more appearances than any other player with 432 appearances. He won the championship 8 times. He led Dynamo to the [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup]] in 1975 and 1986, scoring a goal in each final. Blokhin is also the USSR national football team's most [[cap (sport)|capped]] player with 112 caps, as well as their all-time leading goalscorer with 42 goals; he played in the [[1982 FIFA World Cup|1982]] and [[1986 FIFA World Cup|1986]] [[FIFA World Cup]]s where he scored one goal in each. He was one of the first Soviet players to play abroad, signing for Austria's [[Vorwärts Steyr]] in 1988, he also played in Cyprus with [[Aris Limassol|Aris]].

In 1979 Blokhin played a couple of games for [[Ukraine national football team|Ukraine]] at the Spartakiad of the Peoples of the USSR.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://football.lg.ua/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=6685:1979spartakiadanarodovsssrros&catid=212:sovietua79&Itemid=775|title=Футбольный турнир VII Летней Спартакиады народов СССР. Составы команд.|date=19 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150319200631/http://football.lg.ua/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=6685:1979spartakiadanarodovsssrros&catid=212:sovietua79&Itemid=775|archive-date=19 March 2015}}</ref>

== Managerial career ==
After retiring as a player, Blokhin coached Greek clubs [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] (Under him they won the [[Greek Football Cup|Greek Cup]] and the [[Greek Super Cup]] in 1992), [[PAOK FC|PAOK]], [[AEK Athens F.C.|AEK Athens]], and [[Ionikos F.C.|Ionikos]].

He began serving as the head coach of the [[Ukraine national football team|Ukraine national team]] in September 2003.<ref>{{cite news|title=Blokhin takes Ukraine reins|date=18 September 2003|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0254-0d7b34bbfee2-bb822c4175df-1000--blokhin-takes-ukraine-reins/|publisher=Union of European Football Associations|access-date=18 August 2024|archive-date=30 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240730032130/https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0254-0d7b34bbfee2-bb822c4175df-1000--blokhin-takes-ukraine-reins/|url-status=live}}</ref> Under his leadership, Ukraine [[2006 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|qualified]] for a major tournament for the first time as an independent nation, reaching the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]] in Germany. Ukraine reached the quarter-finals of the tournament, losing to eventual champions [[Italy national football team|Italy]]. Following the side's failure to reach [[UEFA Euro 2008]], Blokhin stepped down as coach on 6 December 2007.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120729023939/http://uk.reuters.com/article/worldFootballNews/idUKL0689781720071206|title=Soccer-Blokhin quits as Ukraine coach}} by Mikhail Volobuyev, Gennady Fyodorov and Ken Ferris, [[Reuters]], 6 December 2007</ref>

On 14 December 2007, he was named head coach of [[FC Moscow]].<ref>[http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=490600&cc=5739 FK Moscow hire former Ukraine manager Blokhin] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121002023516/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=490600&cc=5739 |date=2 October 2012 }} ESPNsoccernet 14 December 2007</ref> The club finished 9th (from 16) and after the season ended Blokhin was fired from the club.<ref>[http://www.sports.ru/football/6293328.html Блохин освобожден от обязанностей главного тренера "Москвы"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200922203049/https://www.sports.ru/football/6293328.html |date=22 September 2020 }}. Sports.ru. 26 November 2008. Retrieved 2 January 2011.</ref> At the end of the season, Blokhin announced that if he knew how things would go in FC Moscow, he would have never signed there. This was because the club released many important players without Blokhin's permission yet still had many high expectations.<ref>[http://www.sports.ru/football/6206389.html Олег Блохин: "Если бы знал, как будут делаться дела в команде, то весной бы не пришел в "Москву"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200922120946/https://www.sports.ru/football/6206389.html |date=22 September 2020 }}. Sports.ru. 16 November 2008. Retrieved 2 January 2011.</ref> Others said that the reason Blokhin failed in FC Moscow was that he and the press didn't have a friendly relationship, and because of that the press was constantly attacking Blokhin and that damaged his status among the players.<ref>[http://www.sports.ru/football/6358902.html Геннадий Литовченко: "Говорил Блохину, что его будут травить"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200922121000/https://www.sports.ru/football/6358902.html |date=22 September 2020 }}. Sports.ru. 4 December 2008. Retrieved 2 January 2011.</ref>

On 21 April 2011, Blokhin was again appointed head coach of the Ukraine national team.<ref>[http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,19692_6888233,00.html Ukraine appoint Blokhin] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202141706/http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,19692_6888233,00.html |date=2 February 2017 }}, [[Sky Sports]] (21 April 2011)</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20110426133526/http://football.uk.reuters.com/leagues/european/news/2011/04/21/LDE73K1AD.php Oleg Blokhin appointed Ukraine coach], [[Reuters]] (21 April 2011)</ref> He led the team in [[UEFA Euro 2012]] on home soil, beating [[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden]] but exiting at the [[UEFA Euro 2012 Group D|group stage]] after defeats to [[France national football team|France]] and [[England national football team|England]].
[[file:Pressekonferenz nach dem Fußballländerspiel Österreich-Ukraine (01.06.2012) Oleh Blochin1.jpg|thumb|Blokhin in 2012]]
On 25 September 2012, [[Dynamo Kyiv]] signed Blokhin to lead the club for the next four years.<ref name=BBBIU17414/> His final matches in charge of Ukraine were [[2014 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|World Cup qualifiers]] against [[Moldova national football team|Moldova]] and [[Montenegro national football team|Montenegro]] in October 2012.<ref name=BtillOCNToU>[http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2012/soccer/09/25/dynamo-kiev-oleh-blokhin.ap/index.html Dynamo Kyiv signs Blokhin as coach for 4 years] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120927081913/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2012/soccer/09/25/dynamo-kiev-oleh-blokhin.ap/index.html |date=27 September 2012 }}, [[Sports Illustrated]] (25 September 2012)</ref> Blokhin was dismissed as Dynamo's manager by the club's President [[Ihor Surkis]] on 17 April 2014 because of the "unsatisfactory results of the team".<ref name=BBBIU17414>[http://en.interfax.com.ua/news/sport/201114.html Dynamo president sacks Blokhin for poor performance] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140418220650/http://en.interfax.com.ua/news/sport/201114.html |date=18 April 2014 }}, [[Interfax-Ukraine]] (17 April 2014)</ref> The day before, in a press conference after Dynamo had lost a match against [[Shakhtar Donetsk]], Blokhin had already stated that he had decided to resign.<ref name=BBBIU17414/> Under his leadership Dynamo never qualified (a rare occasion for the club) for the [[UEFA Champions League]] and performed poorly in the [[UEFA Europa League]].<ref name=BBBIU17414/> In his first year his team finished third in the [[Ukrainian Premier League]] and in his second year (when he was fired) Dynamo was seven points behind Ukrainian Premier League leaders [[FC Dnipro Dnipropetrovsk|Dnipro Dnipropetrovsk]] and Shakhtar Donetsk.<ref name=BBBIU17414/>

== Politics ==
In 1998 Blokhin was elected to [[Verkhovna Rada]] (Ukraine's [[parliament]]) for [[Hromada (political party)|Hromada]].<ref name=DenCommi>[http://www.day.kiev.ua/270204/ Oleh Blokhin: "I have scored all of my goals"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240213101854/https://day.kyiv.ua/sites/default/files/css/css_7xpn-3vS_M-yCrWY09l4kKb7kx8js83JLlwigHEzNmE.css |date=13 February 2024 }}, [[Den (newspaper)|Den]] (1998)</ref> He joined Hromada while still being a member of the [[Communist Party of Ukraine]].<ref name=DenCommi/> In March 2002, Blokhin was elected to Verkhovna Rada for a second term. In October 2002, he joined the [[United Social Democratic Party of Ukraine]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Блохін залишає посаду головного тренера збірної України з футболу |url=https://ua.korrespondent.net/ukraine/254918-blohin-zalishae-posadu-golovnogo-trenera-zbirnoyi-ukrayini-z-futbolu |website=[[Korrespondent.net]] |access-date=15 December 2025 |language=ru |date=16 March 2025 |trans-title=Blokhin resigns as head coach of Ukrainian national football team |archive-date=24 April 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260424025022/https://ua.korrespondent.net/ukraine/254918-blohin-zalishae-posadu-golovnogo-trenera-zbirnoyi-ukrayini-z-futbolu |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Family ==
Blokhin's father, Vladimir Blokhin, is a native of [[Moscow]], a veteran of the [[World War II]], survivor of the [[Leningrad blockade]], and a former Soviet law enforcement agent ([[militsiya]]). He later worked as a sports functionary for the republican [[Dynamo (Ukraine)|Dynamo Society]], which is related to law enforcement and the state security forces. Blokhin's mother [[Kateryna Adamenko]] is from Nebrat village in [[Borodianka Raion]], [[Kyiv Oblast]]. She originally worked at a Kyiv sewing factory, but eventually discovered hidden athletic talents and became the Soviet champion in [[track and field]] as well as pentathlon. After retiring from sports, she became a staff member at one of Kyiv's universities.

Blokhin was married to [[Irina Deriugina]], a top coach and former world champion in [[rhythmic gymnastics]], but the couple divorced in the early 1990s. Blokhin and Deriugina have a daughter, singer [[Iryna Blokhina]], who wrote and performed the Euro 2012 anthem.<ref>[http://tabloid.pravda.com.ua/news/4ebd28fd5427b/ Донька Блохіна заспіває гімн "Євро-2012" (The daughter of Blokhin will sing the Euro 2012 anthem)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120704084446/http://tabloid.pravda.com.ua/news/4ebd28fd5427b/ |date=4 July 2012 }} with photo. TabloID. 11 November 2011</ref>

Blokhin and his second wife, Angela, have two daughters, Hanna (born 2001) and Katerina (born 2002).<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.sport-express.ru/newspaper/2002-09-27/10_1/ |script-title=ru:Олег Блохин: Место В Истории |trans-title=Oleg Blokhin: Place in History |work=Sport-Express |author=Yuri Yuris |date=27 September 2002 |access-date=25 February 2015 |language=ru |archive-date=19 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190419045950/https://www.sport-express.ru/newspaper/2002-09-27/10_1/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
